title: Offline Policy Enhancement and Transfer by Combining Experimental and External One-Sided Treatment Data

problem.claim: Offline policy enhancement and transfer must combine an unconfounded but small experimental dataset with a larger external dataset containing observations from only one treatment arm.

gap.claim: Methods using only the experimental dataset may have low accuracy and limited generalizability, while the external one-sided treatment dataset alone cannot identify policy reward.

contributions.claim: A framework combines experimental and external one-sided treatment data to support offline policy enhancement and transfer.
The framework improves offline policy evaluation and learning in the experimental dataset and enables these tasks in the external one-sided treatment dataset.

stated_novelty.claim: The article presents a novel setting for offline policy enhancement and transfer involving experimental and external one-sided treatment datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments report more accurate reward estimation using the proposed methods.
The experiments report that the learned policies closely approximate the theoretically optimal policy.

narrative_sequence.summary: The article defines a setting that combines experimental data with external one-sided treatment data.
The experimental data are unconfounded but small, whereas the external data are larger but contain only one treatment arm.
Experimental-only methods may lack accuracy and generalizability, and external-only data cannot identify policy reward.
The proposed framework uses both datasets for policy enhancement and policy transfer.
Experiments report improved reward estimation and policies close to the theoretically optimal policy.

source_observation.claim: A small unconfounded experimental dataset and a larger one-sided treatment dataset have complementary limitations.

interpretation.claim: Combining datasets with complementary identification and scale properties can address weaknesses that neither dataset resolves alone.

application.claim: When adapting offline policy methods across data distributions, assess whether multiple datasets can jointly support evaluation and learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the framework applies beyond the stated experimental and one-sided treatment data setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proposed estimators, learning algorithms, assumptions, or theoretical results.
The abstract does not provide experiment datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or implementation details.
